standard_position: No non-solicitation clause in the NDA. Employment matters should not be governed by a confidentiality agreement
fallback_positions: Accept a non-solicitation clause limited to: (a) direct, active solicitation only (not unsolicited applications); (b) employees directly involved in the Purpose; (c) duration of the NDA term only
Accept a broader non-solicitation clause provided there is no contractual penalty and the clause does not apply to employees who apply on their own initiative
red_line: Reject any non-solicitation clause that applies to unsolicited applications, covers all employees regardless of involvement, or includes a contractual penalty
decision_logic: Some NDAs include clauses prohibiting one or both parties from soliciting or hiring the other party's employees. While the intent may be reasonable, broadly worded non-solicitation clauses can create liability even when an employee applies on their own initiative or is hired by a department unaware of the NDA. Non-solicitation clauses that are broadly worded (covering all employees, not just those involved in the Purpose), that extend for long periods, or that are accompanied by contractual penalties.
escalation_logic: Any non-solicitation clause with a penalty should be escalated.
rationale: Some NDAs include clauses prohibiting one or both parties from soliciting or hiring the other party's employees.
